theater.name: Houthis / Red Sea
theater.title: Houthis / Red Sea
theater.sub: The options the US has toward the Houthis in Yemen and the Red Sea, and what followed the last times the US did something like each one.
theater.actor: the Houthis or another Iran-backed group
theater.proxy_note: Iran arms the Houthis, so seizures of Iranian arms bound for them are option E. No reply by another Iran-backed group is logged here.
theater.hold_note: Hold cases are weeks, from Nov 20, 2023 on, with no logged US sanctions, naval, strike or posture move. Weeks inside the long stretches of fighting (Jan 12, 2024 - Jan 19, 2025 and Mar 15 - May 6, 2025) are left out, because US activity there was continuous. Most hold weeks fall in 2025-2026 and most have no logged event at all. The log for 2025-2026 records only major events, so a week where "nothing happened" may only be a week where nothing was logged. Read option A as a rough sketch, and do not compare it number-for-number with options that rest on a few well-reported cases.
theater.not_measured: Oil and freight prices, ship insurance costs, harm to ordinary Yemenis and strain with Saudi Arabia are not measured.
theater.under_logged: Some stretches are logged more thinly than others (2025-2026 far less than 2024, and the Sep 2014 - Oct 2016 years only log the big Houthi acts, not the daily fighting with Saudi and Yemeni forces), so "none logged" is not proof nothing happened.

political.other: Share of past cases NOT followed within 14 days by logged talks, a meeting, a formal proposal to or by the Houthis, a ceasefire or a deal between the US and the Houthis (directly or through a mediator such as Oman). UN resolutions, statements, threats and appeals do not count.
political.hold: Share of hold weeks NOT followed within 14 days by logged talks, a meeting, a formal proposal to or by the Houthis, a ceasefire or a deal between the US and the Houthis (directly or through a mediator such as Oman). UN resolutions, statements, threats and appeals do not count.
political.rule: Counts when no talks, meeting, negotiation, formal proposal made to or by the Houthis, ceasefire or deal between the US and the Houthis, directly or through a mediator such as Oman, was logged in the 14 days after. A UN Security Council resolution or other multilateral act, and public statements, threats and appeals, do not count as talks (for example Trump's Jul 21 and Jul 23, 2026 warnings), so a threat alone does not stop a case from counting as a risk on this category. Rule changed on 2026-10-26.

hostile.title: Houthi fighters take much of Sanaa after days of fighting: the defense ministry, army headquarters, parliament, central bank and state radio are seized with little resistance; on Sep 22 they raid the house of General Ali Mohsen al-Ahmar. The same night they sign a UN-brokered deal with the government (#1051)

Houthi fighters take the presidential palace after a brief clash, a day after both sides announced ceasefires. President Hadi is surrounded in his home and resigns two days later. The UN Security Council condemns the violence

A missile hits a weapons depot in Marib province. The UAE blames the Houthis and Houthi media reportedly confirm a Soviet-era Tochka was fired (anonymous officials, AP). Deadliest day for the UAE military; Bahrain also reports five soldiers killed

USS Sirocco seizes 1,500 AK-47s, 200 RPG launchers and 21 heavy machine guns from a stateless dhow, with USS Gravely sent to help (seized Mar 28, announced Apr 4; logged on the announcement date). The Navy says the arms came from Iran and were likely bound for the Houthis. Third allied seizure since late February

The Houthis CLAIM they destroyed an Emirati warship; the UAE says only that a boat under its command was in an 'incident' and that no one died. Video shows the former US Navy ship burning. USNI: the weapon may have been a C-802 anti-ship missile; a US defense official says the attack is tied to the Yemen conflict, not to shipping in general

Two missiles, believed to be Chinese-made C-802s, are fired at the destroyer USS Mason near Bab el-Mandeb; the Mason fires defensive missiles (USNI dates this Oct 9; the Pentagon calls Oct 12 the 'second time in four days')
Second missile attack on the Mason in four days; the Pentagon says at least one missile came from Houthi-controlled territory near Al Hudaydah and the crew used countermeasures

USS Nitze fires Tomahawk missiles at three Houthi-held coastal radar sites; the Pentagon calls them limited self-defense strikes authorized by President Obama. First US shots against the Houthis in Yemen's war

The Mason fires countermeasures at what officials first said were coastal-defense missiles from Yemen, the third reported incident in about a week; US officials later said the first reports were being reassessed

USS Forrest Sherman's boarding team (Navy and Coast Guard) seizes a significant cache of Iranian guided-missile components from a small wooden boat with no flag; officials say the parts were headed to the Houthis in Yemen and were more advanced than parts seized before (seized in late November, announced Dec 4; logged on the announcement date)
USS Normandy's boarding team seizes 150 Iranian-made Dehlavieh anti-tank missiles and other arms from a dhow (seized Feb 9, announced Feb 13; logged on the announcement date). Also Iran log #264

USS Monterey and a Coast Guard boarding team seize thousands of Chinese-type assault rifles, hundreds of machine guns, sniper rifles and rocket launchers and dozens of Russian-made anti-tank missiles from a stateless dhow on May 6-7. NAVCENT's release says the source and destination are still under investigation; AP says the arms were apparently bound for Yemen (announced May 8; logged on the announcement date)

USS Tempest and USS Typhoon find about 1,400 AK-47 rifles and 226,600 rounds on a stateless fishing vessel on Dec 20, and USS O'Kane takes the cargo; NAVCENT says the boat came from Iran on a route used to smuggle arms to the Houthis, but its release does not name a destination (announced Dec 22; logged on the announcement date)

USCGC John Scheuerman and USS The Sullivans, with USS Hurricane, intercept a fishing vessel on Nov 8 and seize more than 70 tons of ammonium perchlorate (a rocket-fuel ingredient) and over 100 tons of urea fertilizer, shipped from Iran to Yemen and believed bound for the Houthis (announced Nov 15; logged on the announcement date)

USS Lewis B. Puller's team boards a fishing trawler on Dec 1 and seizes more than 50 tons of weapons materials, including over 1 million rounds of 7.62 mm ammunition, nearly 7,000 rocket fuses and RPG propellant, moving from Iran to Yemen (announced Dec 3; logged on the announcement date)
US Navy intercepts a fishing vessel carrying 2,116 AK-47s on a route from Iran to Yemen (seized Jan 6, announced Jan 10; logged on the announcement date). Also Iran log #265
A US defense official confirms Houthi forces shot down an MQ-9 Reaper in international airspace off Yemen
Houthis seize the vehicle carrier Galaxy Leader with 25 crew, citing its Israel link; two US defense officials confirm the Houthis seized it
While the Mason responds to the Nov 26 hijacking of the Central Park, at least one ballistic missile from Houthi-held Yemen lands about 10 nautical miles away (01:41 Sanaa time, Nov 27, per CENTCOM)
CENTCOM reports Houthi missiles hit three commercial ships and USS Carney shoots down three drones; CENTCOM says Iran enables the attacks
Houthi missile hits the Maersk Hangzhou; USS Gravely shoots down two more missiles. CENTCOM counts it the 23rd attack on merchant ships in the Red Sea

Helicopters from USS Gravely and USS Eisenhower sink three of four Houthi boats that fired on the Maersk Hangzhou and tried to board; CENTCOM says the crews were killed. Houthis CLAIM ten of their navy members died

Houthis fire 18 drones, 2 anti-ship cruise missiles and 1 anti-ship ballistic missile toward the southern Red Sea; US and UK ships and jets shoot all 21 down. CENTCOM counts it the 26th launch toward Red Sea shipping
USS Laboon, Gravely and Mason, Eisenhower jets and HMS Diamond shoot down all 21 Houthi drones and missiles

First US-UK strikes on Houthi radar, air-defense and missile and drone sites; Biden calls them a defensive action after 27 attacks on shipping. A later PBS report puts it at more than 60 targets at 28 locations
An anti-ship cruise missile is fired from Houthi-held Yemen toward USS Laboon and shot down by a US fighter. First US-acknowledged Houthi targeting after the Jan 12 strikes
CENTCOM says a Houthi missile hits the US-owned and operated Gibraltar Eagle in the southern Red Sea

CENTCOM announces Navy SEALs seized Iranian-made missile parts from a dhow on Jan 11 (logged on the announcement date); two SEALs were lost at sea. First such seizure since Houthi shipping attacks began
A one-way attack drone from Houthi-held Yemen hits the US-owned Genco Picardy
CENTCOM says US forces struck 14 Houthi missiles on launch rails that posed an imminent threat to ships (announced Jan 17; local time may be Jan 18)
Second round of joint US-UK strikes: eight targets including missile launchers, air defenses, radars and buried storage; Tomahawks and Navy jets used
A Houthi missile hits the tanker Marlin Luanda; USS Carney and other coalition ships help
CENTCOM says US and UK forces hit 36 targets at 13 locations: underground storage, command sites, missile systems, drone sites, radars and helicopters
The Rubymar, hit by a Houthi anti-ship ballistic missile on Feb 18, sinks; CENTCOM warns of fertilizer and fuel spill risk
CENTCOM says a Houthi missile hit the bulk carrier True Confidence, the first fatal Houthi strike on shipping
Houthi drone boats hit the Greek-owned Tutor (a photo caption dates the hit to Jun 12); it was reported sunk on Jun 19, the second ship the Houthis have sunk

After repeated Houthi attacks the tanker Sounion, with about 1 million barrels of crude, is on fire; a French destroyer rescues the 29 aboard. The State Department says the Houthis seem set on sinking it
The first of two MQ-9 Reapers the US later confirmed lost to Houthi fire in under a week
The second MQ-9 lost within a week; the Pentagon confirms both on Sep 18 and calls the Houthi claim of 10 Reapers 'not accurate'
Austin says B-2 bombers hit five hardened underground weapons storage sites in Houthi-held Yemen; CENTCOM believes no civilians were killed

CENTCOM says US warplanes hit a missile storage facility and a command-and-control site in Sanaa on Saturday night and early Sunday (Dec 21-22). During the same hours a US cruiser mistakenly shot down a US F/A-18; both pilots survived. Houthis CLAIM they shot it down

Operation Rough Rider opens: US air and naval forces hit dozens of Houthi targets; the Houthi-run health ministry CLAIMS at least 31 killed (another spokesman said 53); first US strikes since the Gaza ceasefire of Jan 19

Houthis CLAIM 18 ballistic and cruise missiles and one drone at the Truman group; a US official said the attack failed; CENTCOM's Grynkewich later said the Houthis missed by over 100 miles; Abdul-Malik al-Houthi says they will target US ships while US strikes continue
A senior defense official says US warships shot down about a dozen Houthi attack drones headed for the Truman group, which was unaffected

US strikes the Ras Isa fuel terminal; CENTCOM says it aimed to cut a fuel source for the Houthis; Houthi-run media CLAIM at least 38 killed and 102 wounded and CENTCOM would not comment on civilian deaths

CENTCOM says Rough Rider has hit 800+ targets and killed hundreds of Houthi fighters and 'numerous Houthi leaders', including senior missile and drone officials, to 'disintegrate' the group; it did not name anyone
Houthi media CLAIM a US strike hit a Saada detention center for African migrants (35 dead, later 68 per the BBC); AFP could not confirm it and CENTCOM was asked for comment
A US official says seven MQ-9 Reapers have gone down since March 15, about $30 million each; he did not say how they were lost
Small boats, then missiles and drones hit the bulk carrier Magic Seas; the crew abandons ship and is rescued; the ship sinks; the Houthis claimed it

Eternity C is attacked for hours and sinks on Jul 9; Reuters reports at least 4 killed and 15 missing early on, with 6 rescued; USNI later counts at least 9 dead, the Houthis' deadliest attack; the Houthis claimed it

CENTCOM announces Yemen's National Resistance Forces seized 750+ tons of Iranian weapons bound for the Houthis (hundreds of missiles, drone engines, radar); the release describes no direct US military role; also relevant to the Iran log's arms-seizure rows (#264, #265)
UKMTO reports an unknown projectile splashing close to the ship on Aug 31; the Houthis announce the attack on Sep 1; the missile missed and all crew are safe
Houthi cruise missile sets the empty cargo ship on fire; crew airlifted off; two crew hurt and one later dies; the Houthis said the owner broke their ban on calling at Israeli ports

Saudi Arabia confirms the Encelia was hit; the Houthis CLAIM missile and drone strikes on it and the tanker Layla; UKMTO reports another tanker hit by an unknown projectile 70 nm southwest of Al Shuqaiq
Also Iran log #98. Houthi attack on Riyadh's King Khalid airport earlier in the week of Oct 10 kills three Saudis including a pilot (date Oct 8 as in the Iran log; NPR says 'earlier that week')
Also Iran log #102. A missile hits the domestic terminals; Saudi civil aviation says 12 killed (incl. one American) and 309 wounded; 291+ flights cancelled
Saudi air defences stop a drone aimed at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield; the energy ministry does not say who launched it; Reuters and CBS report it among Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam (Reuters, Oct 21); Al Jazeera lists Dammam airport among recent Houthi targets

Houthis CLAIM missile and drone attacks on Riyadh airport, Dammam, Najran, Khamis Mushait, oil pipelines and Aden; Saudi Arabia says it intercepted missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu; Saudi-led jets bomb Marib, Taiz and other provinces

Saudi-led forces say they intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh and destroyed two launchers in Sanaa; Riyadh airport had reopened two terminals on Oct 25 and the Houthis warned airlines against using it

Houthis CLAIM attacks on pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and on Riyadh airport; Saudi Arabia did not immediately confirm (Reuters). The Riyadh part may overlap with the coalition's intercept the same day (#1349). The same day Egypt's parliament authorizes military support for Saudi Arabia

Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles fired toward Riyadh; AFP correspondents hear at least eight explosions; alerts for Riyadh, Kharj and Najran. Separately the Houthi-run health ministry CLAIMS Saudi strikes killed 12 in western Yemen

Coalition says it intercepted a Houthi drone in the Mecca region (the Houthis deny it, saying they target only Saudi oil facilities and military bases), a drone near Riyadh and a ballistic missile over southern Saudi Arabia (CBS)

A police official says the Houthis fired two missiles at the presidential palace in Aden; two eyewitnesses saw ambulances enter the compound; CBS notes a Houthi strike on the perimeter of Aden airport on Oct 28
Saudi air defences intercept a drone in the Riyadh region (coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki), who does not say who launched it; CBS reports it amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia

Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki says a drone was intercepted and destroyed over the Mecca region; he does not say where it came from, and the Houthis did not claim it (they have denied targeting Mecca before)
A strike hits a crowded market in Taiz province. The Houthis blame Saudi-led airstrikes; Yemen's government blames a Houthi ballistic missile (Al Jazeera). AP does not name who carried it out
Airstrikes hit homes east of Sanaa; the Houthi-run health ministry blames Saudi warplanes. Saudi Arabia does not comment (Reuters)

The coalition intercepts a wave of Houthi ballistic missiles and a drone aimed at Riyadh, the Eastern Province and the south; debris blows out windows in an Aramco-owned tower in Riyadh's financial district. Houthi spokesman Saree claims strikes on Riyadh airport, Aramco tanks and Abqaiq as retaliation for Saudi strikes near Sanaa and vows more

A Saudi energy ministry official says an attack on the East-West pipeline caused a 'limited fire' that was put out and did not affect operations; Saudi Arabia does not name the attacker (the Houthis have hit the pipeline before)

The coalition says it shot down a ballistic and a cruise missile over Riyadh and a second ballistic missile over the south; residents get shelter alerts. Houthi spokesman Saree CLAIMS Riyadh and Aramco's Abqaiq site were targeted. The Houthis also report Saudi-led strikes on a gas site and an oil company building in Sanaa (claim)

In an Arabic video, embassy spokesperson Khaled Wolfsberg rejects the Houthi claim of a Saudi blockade, citing 272 commercial ships unloading at Hodeidah, as-Salif and Ras Isa in Jan-Sep 2026, and calls the Houthi siege of Taiz 'the only real blockade'. Words only

The coalition says it intercepted three cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh and drones aimed at Mecca province and the south; Saudi Civil Defence says debris of intercepted ballistic missiles fell in Sabuhah village, Mecca province. The Houthis CLAIM they targeted King Khalid airport and a Yanbu pumping station and call the Mecca claim 'lies'. Houthi shelling and missiles also hit Aden (claim of a hit on a coalition command centre)

The coalition says it intercepted drones over the Riyadh region and the Eastern Province. Saree CLAIMS hits on an East-West pipeline pumping station, Yanbu, a cargo plane at Sharurah, Khamis Mushait airbase and Aramco's Riyadh headquarters; none is confirmed

The coalition says it intercepted two suspected Houthi drones on Nov 14, then two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and three drones over the Eastern Region on Nov 15. Saudi authorities say at least 26 people have been killed in Saudi Arabia by suspected Houthi attacks since Sep 23. The US Embassy in Riyadh issues a nationwide alert urging 'heightened vigilance' over Houthi attacks
Houthi health authorities say Saudi drone and air strikes hit a house in Sanaa and a fuel station in Omran; Saudi Arabia does not comment (AP; reports a Houthi claim)
Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki says a Houthi drone was 'intercepted and destroyed in Riyadh Region'

Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki says a 'precision operation' hit 60 Houthi military targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah, Amran and Saada, including tunnels used as ballistic-missile workshops (announced Nov 18). No casualty figures

AFP reports 'a powerful explosion' in Riyadh and smoke near the airport; the coalition says it intercepted two cruise missiles, and alerts go out in Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait. Houthi spokesman Saree CLAIMS hits on the airport and the financial centre with 'a large number of cruise missiles'; no Saudi confirmation of hits (Reuters). The coalition later says it destroyed a ballistic-missile launch platform in Saada

A Houthi missile hits the tower of the Public Investment Fund, Riyadh's tallest building, damaging several floors and nearby buildings; the district is closed. The coalition says it intercepted four ballistic missiles aimed at the south and two drones later. Saudi Arabia says it has 'full and legitimate right to take all necessary measures'

Saudi Arabia says the Houthis fired more missiles and drones; the coalition says it intercepted five drones and ballistic missiles over Jizan (debris in Al-Shuqaiq) and toward Riyadh. The Houthis CLAIM 'accurate and direct' hits on the Al-Shuqaiq power station and Jizan port

After telling civilians to leave the port area, the coalition says it hit Hodeidah port facilities 'used in smuggling operations' and Houthi missile and drone capabilities in Sanaa, with operations in Saada and Taiz. Al Jazeera's reporter calls them the heaviest air strikes since the conflict began. No casualty figures
Houthi authorities accuse Saudi forces of killing 19 people on a civilian boat. The accusation is not confirmed (CBS News; reports a Houthi claim)
The coalition says it destroyed a drone launched toward Riyadh and intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at the western region
The Houthi-side health ministry reports a strike on a fuel station on 60th Street in Sanaa; the coalition did not comment (Al Jazeera; reports a Saba claim; CBS News; reports a Houthi claim)
Houthi media report a strike on a telecom building in Hodeidah; 'Riyadh didn't immediately comment on the report' (CBS News; reports a Houthi media claim)

Houthi-side authorities report people killed and hurt: six injured at a Sanaa fuel station (Nov 22, #1379), four killed and 18 wounded at a Hodeidah telecom building (Nov 23, #1380) and 19 killed on a civilian boat (Nov 20, #1381). These are claims; the coalition had not commented and none is confirmed.

A Houthi drone aimed at Riyadh was destroyed and a ballistic missile aimed at the western region was intercepted on Nov 22; no casualties or damage were reported (#1378). The Houthi threat to Saudi airspace and Red Sea ports from Nov 20 is still open (#1375).

No US move against the Houthis was found: no strike, sanctions, naval action or talks, and the coverage read names no US role in the Saudi strikes. Reuters' sources said on Nov 19 that Trump has not agreed to US strikes and the US gives intelligence and targeting help (#1372).

theater.sub: A shared case library, not a country tab: US operations from 1983 to 2026 that captured or killed a country's leader or a top leader of an armed group, cartel or terror group, with the pressure steps around them, and what the target's side did after (attacks, protests, talks).
theater.proxy_note: The target's side is whoever the operation was aimed at: the leader's government, group or cartel, and sometimes the host country. A reply is counted only when the log links it to the US move or it falls inside the window. Statements by blocked state or armed-group media are never cited.
theater.hold_note: Option A has no cases here. There is no single conflict to count quiet weeks in: a week with no US raid against one leader says nothing about another. NAPOR does not invent hold weeks, so the page shows option A as having too few cases.
theater.not_measured: Economic effects (sanctions, trade, prices) are not measured for these past cases; that category is left out of the index. Strain with host countries is shown only as logged protests and breaks in relations.
theater.under_logged: The log is a sample of well-documented operations that have a working link in an allowed outlet or official source. Some operations (for example partner captures where no allowed page states the US role) are left out, and most of the rows have not been checked for a reply 30 days after, so "none logged" is not proof nothing happened.

cases.kind: Diplomatic talks (US negotiates privately with Noriega's side on his stepping down)
cases.title: May 17: Reagan says the US is negotiating with Panama but will not discuss it and that the goal is 'a restoration of democracy'. CSM (May 24): the US bypassed Panama's opposition coalition and negotiated privately with Noriega; National Security Adviser Colin Powell indicated the US might drop two indictments if he resigned as defense force commander. CSM (May 20): leaks about dropping the indictments; Vice President Bush said he would never 'bargain' with drug dealers. Logged on the day Reagan confirmed the talks; they had started earlier
cases.note: US-Noriega talks confirmed May 17, 1988; they failed about May 27 (#5013). Searched to Jun 16: GAO's 1988 chronology (Jul 26, 1989) lists the US ending the talks (May 25) and new US sanctions rules (Jun 3, Jun 10, Jun 23) and no attack on US people by Noriega's side; CSM, May 27, says only that the talks failed. No attack reported.

The State Department historian: it called for President Aristide's return by Oct 30, 1993. AP (1994): Cedras had broken earlier promises to leave
cases.note: Governors Island Agreement, Jul 3, 1993 -> the military broke up pro-Aristide demonstrations by force and detainees were beaten in custody (UN-OAS official Ian Martin, CSM Jul 19, day 16; #5050); the UN-OAS mission counted about 50 killings between Jul 1 and August, mostly by armed gangs with close military ties (CSM Sep 17). People hurt: yes. US forces hit: no. No page ties the violence to the accord in the attackers' words. The Oct 11 Harlan County incident (#5033) is day 100, outside the window.

Searched to Nov 11: Aidid orders his men to stop fighting and frees Durant on Oct 14 (#5035); CSM, Oct 18: his gunmen held their fire; CSM, Nov 8 (day 27): no new attacks on US or UN troops in late Oct and early Nov, and US talks with Aidid's senior aides revived (Oakley's second visit). cases.kind: Raid (air interception forces the EgyptAir plane carrying the Achille Lauro hijackers to land at Sigonella)
cases.title: At the President's direction US F-14s from the carrier Saratoga find the aircraft and escort it to the Sigonella air base in Italy without firing a shot (White House statement). It lands with Italian consent and the hijackers go into Italian custody. CSM: the plane had left Egypt carrying the hijackers, Egyptian officials and two PLO leaders. The US later named PLF leader Muhammad Abbas as the mastermind (#5006). Partial capture: the hijackers were held, the leader was not
cases.note: Achille Lauro interception, Oct 10, 1985. Oct 11-13: the Sigonella standoff and Italy letting Abbas go (#5005, #5006) are diplomatic rows with the host government. Nothing found by Abbas's side in the window (searched to Nov 9): the State Department's 1985 chronology of American-related terrorist incidents (read via ojp.gov) lists three incidents Oct 10 - Nov 9 (bombs in Concepcion and Santiago, Chile, Oct 23 and 28; an Army recruiting officer shot in San Juan, Puerto Rico, Nov 6), none tied to Abbas or the PLF. CSM, Oct 21 and Oct 24, warn of more attacks on Americans but report none. No attack reported.

cases.kind: Raid (Rangers' raid in central Mogadishu turns into a 17-hour battle; two helicopters downed)

US losses on Oct 3-4 (18 killed, 84 wounded) and Durant's capture are the operation itself; he was freed Oct 14 (#5035). CSM, Oct 18: Aideed's gunmen held their fire under two cease-fires. CSM, Nov 8 (day 36): no new attacks on US or UN troops in late Oct and early Nov. People hurt: yes. US forces hit: yes.
